title: Clothing Making
text: “Well, I can see why they’re growing so fast. So their lives are destined to burn out in an instant…”
“Look at how much they’ve grown in just three days… I see…”
My father and Éclair are watching Yuki-chan and the others with sad expressions on their faces.
“That’s not it at all!”

It seems my father has misunderstood something. Thinking they’re going to die is quite a grim misunderstanding. And for Éclair to just accept that so rudely! Motoyasu, your explanation was insufficient.
“An ‘angel’ literally means that Filolial-sama becomes an angel. That’s why we’re securing the equipment.”
“Oh, I see. That surprised me. Equipment?”
“It’s equipment that turns Magical Power into clothing.”
“Ah, I’ve heard of that. It’s for Demi-Humans with transformation abilities in Siltvelt and Shieldfreeden, right?”
It seems Éclair understands.
“It would be great if they sold it in a town around here…”
“We’ll have to look for it in the neighboring towns.”

In the first world, when I consulted a monster merchant, they explained the equipment to me and placed an order for it. But in this loop, that probably won’t be possible. So we’ll need to go to the neighboring towns and see if we can find such equipment.
“Shall we assist you in securing those items?”
“Is that even possible?”

Come to think of it, Siltvelt was a country of Demi-Humans. That means there must be a large number of Demi-Humans with transformation abilities. Given their extensive connections, it’s not out of the question. Perhaps they could create clothing far more sophisticated and exquisite than anything in Melromarc—clothing that brings out Filolial-sama’s charm to the absolute limit. My heart is racing.
“While I’m at it, I’ll try to get in touch with the home country.”
“Hmm… We really need to do something about our pursuers, but no matter how many we defeat, more keep appearing. If the Siltvelt Army protects Lord Iwatani, the danger should be reduced.”
Éclair’s point is well taken.
“I believe that worry will be resolved to some extent if we can just get through today. After all, if we can raise Father’s level, it’ll become much harder for anyone to harm him.”
“U-uh-huh. I’ll do my best.”
“Yuki-chan. Sakura-chan. You two must protect Father.”
Yuki-chan and Sakura-chan respond by cheerfully raising their wings. It’s a wonderful sight—a perfect blend of cuteness and reliability.
“Alright, let’s get started!”
At my signal, Yuki-chan and Sakura-chan let out cheerful cries and took off running.
“Whoa! They’re so fast!”
“They’re going to fall! Speed up a little more—”
“Oink—”
The sight of them racing off with my Father and the others aboard is truly majestic. I climbed into the makeshift carriage alongside the messenger from Siltvelt.
“Well then, let’s set off for the nearest town!”
“Guaaaaaaah!”
As I gripped the reins tightly, Kou set off energetically. This sensation of cutting through the wind—dada-dada—is a thrill like no other.

I went to the nearest town with the envoy from Siltvelt. It seems we’re already approaching this country’s capital. On the map, it appears to be a small country situated between Melromarc and Siltvelt. Unfortunately, I’m told they don’t have any Dragon Hourglasses.
“Do you know anything about this country, Spear Hero?”
“I don’t, actually.”

The truth is, I only know Melromarc, Faubrey, and maybe Zeltoble. I’ve stopped by a few places along the way, but unfortunately, I’ve never been to this area before. Thinking back to when it was a game might be helpful, but since the reliability of my gaming knowledge is questionable—especially after talking with my Father—it’s probably best to see it with my own eyes.

“I see… This country has a short history, and because it’s small, it lacks national power. Due to its location, where conflicts often arise between Demi-Humans and humans… during times of war, it becomes a battleground where our country and our arch-rival, Melromarc, vie for control.”
I see. It doesn’t seem very wealthy. Come to think of it, what’s the situation with food supplies? It looks rather run-down at first glance.
“Do they have any local specialties?”
If it’s food, I’ll consider bringing some back as souvenirs for Yuki-chan and the others.
“I haven’t really heard of any. Since it’s a country that developed through trade… it’s a place well-suited for buying goods from other nations.”
“Hmm…”

I see. So, perhaps the residents of Melromarc use this country as a middleman to purchase goods that can only be harvested in Siltvelt? If that’s the case, it’s essentially a lower-tier version of Zeltoble. Racking my brain for memories from when this was a game… was there even a town around here?

I remember now. If I’m not mistaken, it was a small, local—or rather, a waystation—town. It wasn’t that there were no events, but the main attraction was just the instant dungeons. However, since this world isn’t a game, there’s no need to go into dungeons. Venturing in to hunt for rare items or gear is one option, but… as things stand, my Father and the others don’t have any issues with their current gear.
“Is there any equipment here that can turn Magical Power into fabric?”
“I plan to check with our branch office back home, just in case.”
“Understood.”
And so, I headed to the branch office with the messenger. Fortunately, we found the equipment we were looking for.
“Now we just need to turn the thread into fabric, but we’ll have to hire a professional for that, won’t we?”
“That’s right. Can we get that done in this town?”
“Yes. I hear there’s a shop here that will turn it into fabric quickly—as long as you pay them.”
With this, everything will be taken care of.
“Then let’s get a sewing kit. I’ll be the one to turn the finished fabric into clothes.”
“…Will the Spear Hero be making the clothes?”
“Did I say something strange?”

It seems this messenger doesn’t know who sewed the clothes for Filolial-sama and the others. I, Motoyasu, am quite skilled at making clothes. I’ve honed my eye for fashion and my sewing skills by studying fashion magazines in the past, and I’m confident that in this area, at least, I’m every bit as good as my Father.

To tell you the truth, it was this Motoyasu who hand-sewed Filolial-sama and the others’ clothes. Also, I made Filo-tan’s life-size doll myself. Even I have to admit it was such a magnificent creation that I slept next to it every night.
“N-no…”
Anyway, with this, I’m all set to procure Filolial-sama’s clothes. Perhaps I should buy a generously sized cloak just in case it gets torn.
“Guh… Kue!”
It seems Kou has fully transformed into his Filolial King form. He looks absolutely adorable. The envoy from Siltvelt is tilting his head in wonder as he looks at Kou.
“Is this… the King of Filolial from the legends… like a divine bird?”
“That’s right!”
“Whoa!”
The envoy was so startled he fell backward. What on earth is he so surprised about?
“Filolial-sama is a divine bird, you know!”
“Ah, yes. That’s right.”
“Guaaaaaa…”

As I stroke Kou’s throat, I ponder what lies ahead. I’ve already procured everything I need. All that’s left is to wait for my Father and the others to return, but is there anything else I should be doing? Just as I’m thinking this, the envoy from Siltvelt furrows his brow upon receiving a report from the branch office.
“What’s the matter?”
“No… I’ve heard there are signs of unrest beginning to emerge in Melromarc.”
“I believe assassins have already been sent here multiple times.”
“Outwardly, they’ve been pretending to be uninvolved… but apparently, they’ve sent a letter of regret to Siltvelt, using the excuse that the Shield Hero destroyed the border as a pretext.”

Good grief. They launched a hostile attack themselves, and now that they’ve been defeated, they’re trying to pick a fight. They’re truly despicable to the core. If my father-in-law and the others hadn’t stopped me, I, Motoyasu, would be charging through the portal right now to slaughter the Trash.
“Our country’s leadership is attending a global conference in preparation for the wave, and they’re currently verifying the facts with that vixen from Melromarc…”
“Shall we attack and destroy Melromarc?”
“I imagine it would be quite difficult to outwit that she-fox and the Wise King. A rash invasion could turn not only our allies but the entire world against us.”

It seems that Trash still holds some authority. Come to think of it, I recall the Crimson Swine boasting in the past about how he once outmaneuvered Siltvelt with his cunning… I’ve heard that he was forced to prostrate himself before my Father and was bestowed the title of “Trash.” I would have loved to have been there to witness that.
“Hahahaha, I don’t think there’s any need to worry. I, Motoyasu, will slaughter all of Father’s enemies right before your eyes.”

“We’ve witnessed the strength of the Spear Hero ourselves, so we won’t deny it. However, our nation’s leadership hasn’t seen it, so we’re not in a position to take action just yet. Please bear with us a little longer.”
It seems some troublesome procedures are required.
“Besides… it’s true that the waves are causing great turmoil in the country… As the legends say, we must face the waves alongside the Shield Hero.”
“That’s right. It’s a more important issue than war.”
“Let’s make delivering the Shield Hero our top priority. The nation’s leadership will decide what comes next.”
The messenger clenched his fist as he replied.
“I have no authority to decide on war… Beyond Melromarc’s female fox’s official policy, there is the debt of gratitude left by Seaetto. Siltvelt will simply welcome the Shield Hero with open arms.”
And now, the messenger is offering some sort of prayer. He must be thinking of his Father. If so, this man is likely trustworthy. He is a slave, after all, and doesn’t seem to be lying.
“What shall we do next?”
“Our business here is finished. However…”
The messenger glanced briefly toward the shadow of the building. I had the feeling a figure was hiding there.
“Shall we chase after him and take him out?”
“Since we haven’t confirmed he’s a Melromarc assassin, let’s let him go for now. We’re gradually gathering allies of our own as well.”
“Understood. Then let’s return to where we parted ways.”
And so, I found myself waiting for my Father to return.
